content.title: Cameron and Cayden Boozer's mother talks Duke stars
content.text: CeCe Boozer has been a major supporter of her twin sons and Duke stars Cameron and Cayden throughout their careers.Both Cameron and Cayden have become two of the biggest stars in this year’s NCAA tournament as No. 1-seeded Duke advanced to the second weekend of the Big Dance. Their mom talked with the Grownwoman podcast before the season in May 2025 about how she raised the twins and their older brother, Carmani, who plays baseball at the University of Fort Lauderdale.“I think it feels a little bit surreal because when you’re in the moment of making the sacrifice, you don’t think it’s a sacrifice,” CeCe Boozer said during the podcast. “You just go with where your heart is.”More News: Fans Pour Out Support For Vanderbilt Star Amid Big MissCameron Boozer #12 talks with Cayden Boozer #2 of the Duke Blue Devils before their game against the UCF Knights at Cameron Indoor Stadium on October ...More News: Analyst Touts 'Troll Job' During VCU-Illinois GameCeCe Boozer married former NBA player Carlos Boozer in 2002, and they had three children before their divorce in 2015. She had her own athletic success as a college volleyball player, and she works in the business now.“And I tell people that all the time when they ask, like, how do you do this or how do you do that? And I said, because it’s the only thing I know,” she said. “I put my head down, and I do the work, and I see the goal, and I meet the goal.”Cameron Boozer #12 looks on with Cayden Boozer #2 of the Duke Blue Devils during their game against the UCF Knights at Cameron Indoor Stadium on Octob...“And once I meet the goal, I make another goal. For me, it’s nice to see them at this moment, seeing the culmination of everything that’s happened and to be able to look back and say, ‘I’m thankful, and I’m grateful for you kind of putting your head down and making the way,’” she added. “So I think that as a parent, that’s all we can ask for.”Cameron Boozer, a high NBA draft prospect, averages 22.4 points and 10.3 points per game for the Blue Devils. Cayden Boozer averages 7.4 points and 2.2 rebounds per game.More News: Michigan Star Given 2-Word Nickname After Highlight Dunks​
